newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks surge late to close on record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks surge late to close on record high.

text.p: Swiss shares shrugged off morning doldrums to gain power in the afternoon on Monday and close above the prior record of 3,813.6 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) set in July.
Dealers said the index surged due to buying in shares with a heavy SMI weighting.
More advances were possible in the near future, one trader said. "But the air is getting a little thin", he added.
The SMI gained 0.31 percent, or 11.7 points, to a record closing high of 3,813.7. The intra-day high was at 3,819.2.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 8.14 points, or 0.33 percent, to 2,440.05 points.
Volumes were described as comparatively high.
Trade was particularly active in Nestle shares, which gained 18 francs or 1.29 percent to 1,409 francs. Dealers said the market was realising that Nestle had long been neglected.
Surveillance also caught up with the market's recent advance, jumping almost two percent to 2,880 francs.
Roche continued last week's advances, putting on 45 francs to 9,605. Clariant shares were also higher.
Among financials, CS Holding and Swiss Re were among the losers.
CS Holding sank 0.75 francs to 128 due to switches to SBC and UBS, which both gained 0.8 percent, a dealer said. SBC hit a year's high at 251 francs.
Shares of personnel services firm Adia were sought by several banks after a road show and a recommendation by UBS, one dealer said. Adia rose 14 francs at 360.
Second-tier Keramik Laufen fell six francs to 699. The firm said that talks with Dutch Sphinx about a partial cooperation have been broken off.
